snippet.title: Battle City (Famicom, 1985) – 2 Loop High Score Session (1P) + Construction + Easter Egg 🦅🏗️🥚
snippet.description:
🔔 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMpNLYz8bcz1-i2vWxSEieQ?sub_confirmation=1

*🎮 Title:* バトルシティー (BattleCity) 
*_🕹 Platform Spec_*  
 *🖥️ System:* Nintendo Family Computer (Famicom, FC)
 *🌍 Region Label:* JP 🇯🇵
 *📄 Revision:* Original
 *📅 Release:* 1985-September-09
 *🏢 Publisher:* Namcot
 *👾 Developer:* Namco

*_🔁 Port Info_*
 *• Type:* Remake / Rebuild (Re‑engineered Arcade Conversion)
 *• Origin:* Tank Battalion (Arcade, Japan, 1980)

*🎲 Genre:* Action → Shooter → Multidirectional Shooter (Fixed‑screen)

*_🧮 Score Profile_*
 *⭐️ Personal Score:* A
 *🌐 Consensus Score:* B+ (▲)
 *💬 Cultural Impact (Ψ):* A– (✓)
 *📆 Historical Tier:* B+ (↑)

*✅ Completion Status:* 2× Loop Clear → loop definition: 35 Stages / High Score Session (441,900pts)
*🏁 Ending Type:* No Ending

*_🔥 Difficulty Profile_*
*📈 Difficulty Curve:* Gradual + Loop Increase (With Spikes)
*⚙️ Perceived Global Difficulty:* Reasonable + Endurance 
 
*🧠 Play Mode:* Focused Play
*🎯 Intent:* Documentation


This second *Battle City* video expands experience across two full difficulty loops and includes demonstrations of the *Construction* mode and a hidden *Easter egg* 🕹️. As always, you control a Player Tank on fixed‑screen arenas built from Field Characters (tiles) such as Brick, Bulletproof Wall, River, Forest, Ice Field, and Blank. The objective remains constant: destroy all 20 enemy tanks in each stage while preventing any projectile from striking the Headquarters. If the Headquarters is hit or all Player Tanks are lost, the game ends instantly with a GAME OVER screen 🎯. There is no narrative ending; the game loops indefinitely, restarting after each 35‑stage cycle.

The Player Tank upgrades through Stars, progressing from Normal Tank to Rapid‑Fire Tank, Double‑Shot Tank, and Super Tank, the only form capable of destroying Bulletproof Walls. Enemy types—Light Tank, Armored Vehicle, Rapid‑Fire Tank, and Heavy Tank—define the pacing and pressure of each stage. Flashing enemies drop items such as Hand Grenade, Helmet, Schop (Shovel), Tank (1‑Up), and Clock, each granting 500 points and shaping the scoring rhythm. The game supports cooperative play, but this session is strictly 1‑Player.

What distinguishes this video is its structural scope: it completes 70 stages, covering both the base difficulty loop (Stages 1–35) and the harder second loop (Stages 36–70). After Stage 70, the internal counter resets to “1” and the difficulty returns to its initial baseline, confirming that escalation is loop‑bounded rather than exponential. The Difficulty Curve for this extended session is Gradual + Loop Increase (With Spikes), while the Perceived Global Difficulty becomes Reasonable + Endurance due to the cumulative strain of surviving two full loops. The session ends early in Loop 3 when I intentionally destroy my own Headquarters, making this a 2× Loop Clear + Survival Session + High Score Session.

This video also highlights the Construction mode, where you design custom stages by placing tiles with a tank‑shaped cursor and assigning an existing Stage Number’s Enemy Tank Organization. It also includes the game’s secret message easter egg, triggered by repeatedly entering and exiting Construction and then performing a specific sequence of directional holds and button presses across both controllers. As in the first video, Battle City remains a remake‑type adaptation of Namco’s Tank Battalion, rebuilt with new code, destructible environments, power‑ups, cooperative play, and a stage editor. My Personal Score of A reflects its mechanical clarity and expressive design, while external consensus places it at B+ with strong cultural resonance in bootleg and multicart contexts. This second video captures the game’s long‑form endurance challenge and its creative potential beyond standard stages.

#BattleCity #バトルシティー #BattleCityNES #BattleCityFamicom
